meta.sous_theme: Egg structure, changes with age, uses in cooking

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A woman in Limbe buys a tray of eggs on Monday and uses the last ones on Saturday, and she wants to know whether they are still good. Eggs feed the family, make cakes rise, thicken sauces and hold fishcakes together. Because they are used in so many dishes, the GCE asks about their structure, how they change as they age, and their uses in cooking.

items: Protein sets (coagulates) when it is heated.
Water can evaporate slowly through tiny holes.
Bacteria multiply in warm conditions and can make food unsafe.

sections.titre: Egg cookery: structure, ageing, freshness test and uses in cooking
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Structure of an egg
| Part | Description and function |
|---|---|
| Shell | hard, porous, made mainly of calcium carbonate; protects the egg and lets air pass through its pores |
| Cuticle (bloom) | thin transparent protective coating on the shell; seals the pores against bacteria and slows water loss |
| Shell membranes | two thin layers under the shell; a barrier to bacteria |
| Air cell | a pocket of air between the membranes at the blunt end |
| White (albumen) | thick and thin white; mainly water and protein |
| Chalazae | twisted cords that hold the yolk in the centre |
| Yolk | fat, protein, vitamins A and D, iron; held in a thin yolk membrane |

An egg gives protein of high quality, fat, iron and several vitamins. It contains almost no carbohydrate and no vitamin C.

### Changes as an egg gets older
1. Water evaporates through the pores, so the air cell grows larger.
2. The egg becomes lighter.
3. The white becomes thin and watery.
4. The yolk flattens.
5. The yolk moves off centre.
6. The yolk membrane weakens, so the yolk breaks easily.
7. The flavour weakens, bacteria can enter through the pores, and a very old egg smells unpleasant.

### Testing freshness
Place the egg in a bowl of cold water. A fresh egg sinks and lies flat. An older egg tilts or stands on its end. A very old egg floats because its air cell is large.

### Storage
Store eggs in a cool place or a refrigerator with the pointed end down, away from strong-smelling food, because the shell lets smells in. Do not wash them before storage, as this removes the cuticle.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for the uses or importance of egg in a dish or a cake mixture.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name the function and give a dish for it: **aerating** (whisked egg traps air in sponges and meringues); **coagulating or setting** (custard, baked egg dishes); **binding** (fishcakes); **thickening** (custard and sauces); **emulsifying** (yolk holds oil and vinegar together in mayonnaise); **coating** (egg and breadcrumbs before frying); **glazing** (brushing pastry); **enriching** (adds protein, vitamins, colour and flavour); **garnishing** (slices of boiled egg). In a cake mixture the egg traps air, helps the cake to rise, binds the ingredients, sets the structure when baked, and adds colour, flavour and food value.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how to boil, fry, poach or scramble an egg, or why an egg is overcooked.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Boil: lower the egg gently into simmering water (about 3 to 4 minutes for soft, about 10 to 12 minutes for hard). Poach: slide it into gently simmering water. Fry, scramble and make omelettes in a little hot fat, stirring scrambled egg gently. Overcooking makes the white rubbery, and a long boil gives a grey-green ring round the yolk; cooling a hard-boiled egg in cold water at once helps to prevent it. Gentle heat gives the best texture.

sections.enonce_markdown: A student wants to know whether an egg bought a week ago is still fresh. Describe a simple test and explain what the result shows about the egg. (6 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "Describe" asks for what is done, in order. "Explain" asks for the reason behind the result. Six marks suggest three marks for each part.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Part 1: the steps of the test. Part 2: the reasons for each result.

etapes.justification: The method must be clear enough for someone else to repeat.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Half-fill a clean bowl with cold water and place the egg gently in it. Look at how it lies.

etapes.justification: Each result tells a different age.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A fresh egg sinks and lies flat. An older egg tilts or stands on its end. A very old egg floats.

etapes.justification: The reason links the result to a change in the egg.
etapes.resultat_markdown: As an egg ages, water evaporates through the pores of the shell and the air cell grows larger, so the egg becomes lighter and rises in the water.

etapes.justification: Marks often go for a sensible decision.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A floating egg should be thrown away; an egg that stands on its end should be cooked soon and well.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Test:** place the egg in a bowl of cold water. It sinks and lies flat if fresh, tilts or stands up if older, and floats if very old. **Explanation:** with age, water evaporates through the shell, the air cell grows and the egg becomes lighter. A floating egg should be thrown away.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that the shell of an egg is smooth and has no holes.
items.pourquoi_faux: The shell is porous. Air passes through, water evaporates from the egg, and bacteria can enter.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the shell is porous, and that the cuticle seals the pores.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that the yolk is held in place by the shell membrane.
items.pourquoi_faux: The shell membranes lie under the shell. The yolk is held in the centre by the chalazae.
items.correction_markdown: Name the chalazae as the cords that hold the yolk in position.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving "the egg gets bigger" or "the egg becomes heavier" as a change in an older egg.
items.pourquoi_faux: Water is lost, so the egg becomes lighter and the air cell becomes bigger, not the egg.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the air cell enlarges and the egg becomes lighter.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing "eggs are cheap" and "eggs taste nice" as the importance of egg in a cake.
items.pourquoi_faux: The question asks for the work that the egg does in the mixture.
items.correction_markdown: Write aerating, binding, setting, and adding colour, flavour and food value.

items.erreur_markdown: Boiling an egg hard for twenty minutes to be sure that it is safe.
items.pourquoi_faux: Long boiling makes the white rubbery and gives a grey-green ring round the yolk.
items.correction_markdown: Boil for about 10 to 12 minutes, then cool it in cold water.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Name the part of an egg that holds the yolk in the centre. (b) State the function of the air cell. (c) Name two nutrients that the yolk supplies.
items.solution_markdown: (a) The **chalazae**. (b) The air cell is a pocket of air at the blunt end; it grows as the egg ages and so shows how old the egg is. (c) Any two of: **fat, protein, iron, vitamin A, vitamin D.**

items.enonce_markdown: A tray of 30 eggs costs $3\,000$ FCFA. A cake recipe uses 4 eggs and the cake is cut into 16 equal slices. (a) Find the cost of one egg. (b) Find the cost of the eggs in one cake. (c) Find the cost of eggs per slice. (d) A caterer bakes 6 such cakes. How many eggs are used, what is their cost, and how many eggs remain from the tray?
items.solution_markdown: (a) $3\,000 \div 30 = 100$, so **100 FCFA**. (b) $4 \times 100 = 400$, so **400 FCFA**. (c) $400 \div 16 = 25$, so **25 FCFA** per slice. (d) Eggs used: $6 \times 4 = 24$, so **24 eggs**. Cost: $24 \times 100 = 2\,400$, so **$2\,400$ FCFA**. Remaining: $30 - 24 = 6$, so **6 eggs**.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain the part played by egg in each of these: (a) mayonnaise, (b) fishcakes, (c) a whisked sponge cake, (d) a baked egg custard. Then give three rules for storing eggs and say why each is important.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Mayonnaise: the yolk is an emulsifier and holds the oil and vinegar together. (b) Fishcakes: egg binds the mixture, and egg and breadcrumbs make a coating that gives a crisp surface when fried. (c) Sponge: whisked egg traps air, which expands in the oven and raises the cake; the egg protein then sets the structure. (d) Custard: the egg proteins coagulate when baked and set the custard. Storage rules: keep eggs in a cool place or a refrigerator, to slow ageing and the growth of bacteria; keep them pointed end down so that the yolk stays central; keep them away from strong-smelling foods, because the shell lets smells pass in. (Do not wash them first, because that removes the protective cuticle.)

items_markdown: Learn the parts: shell, cuticle, shell membranes, air cell, white, chalazae, yolk; the shell is porous and the cuticle protects it.
An older egg has a larger air cell, is lighter, has a thin watery white and a flat yolk that moves off centre and breaks easily.
Water test: a fresh egg sinks and lies flat, an older egg tilts, a very old egg floats.
Egg functions: aerating, setting, binding, thickening, emulsifying, coating, glazing, enriching and garnishing; give a dish for each.
Cook eggs gently; overcooking toughens the white and gives a grey-green ring round a hard-boiled yolk.
Store eggs cool, pointed end down, away from strong smells, and unwashed.
